title: Lighting the rock, underground
question: One of these has light on the stone — shaded undersides, lit tops, a dark line where rock meets air. Which one, and is it better or does it look wrongly 3D?
context_md:
Lane D, testing one claim: *adding real shading to terrain is the cheapest large gain available, and it is not a worldgen change*.

Both panes are the same world, same instant, same camera, same palette. The only difference is a light applied over the top — colours come from the shipped renderer, so neither pane can show a colour the engine would not have drawn.

**Asking here rather than at the surface on purpose.** Light can only do something where rock meets air, and underground **22%** of the stone on screen is near an opening against **5%** at the surface — so this is the best case this idea will ever get. There is a companion card of the same knob at the surface.

Two earlier answers make me wary of it: the depth grade you played and rejected (*"no question grade off is better"*), and the plant shading you called *"kinda 3d-ish"*. If this reads the same way, say so and I will stop pushing it.

items.label: lit
